question.prompt: Find the sum of the arithmetic series \[ 20+20\frac15+20\frac25+\cdots+40. \]

solutions.explanation:
The terms increase by \(\frac15\), so first count the gaps from \(20\) to \(40\):
\[
\frac{40-20}{1/5}=100.
\]
Including both endpoints gives \(101\) terms.

Pair the first term with the last, the second with the next-to-last, and continue inward. In each pair, the increase from \(20\) matches the decrease from \(40\), so every pair sums to \(60\). The \(101\) terms form \(50\) pairs and leave the middle term, \(30\). Hence the sum is
\[
50\cdot60+30=\boxed{3030},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Count the gaps and pair the terms
